title: Data Preparation and Quality
learning_outcomes: Explain data collection and source selection and how it connects to data preparation and quality.
Apply data cleaning and normalization in the example and predict the output before running it.
Test one realistic edge case for data preparation and quality and explain what the example does not prove.

content.intro: This lesson covers data preparation and quality through 6 syllabus subtopics preserved from the supplied Generative AI curriculum. Revisit mathematical ideas as practical tools for representing data, uncertainty, similarity, and optimization. You can begin using pretrained models before mastering every optional derivation.
content.why_it_matters: Data collection and source selection addresses how information is prepared, described, versioned, or governed. Validate the input, keep source and access metadata, handle duplicates and missing values deliberately, and test the downstream effect of a data change rather than treating the data pipeline as invisible plumbing.

items.text: Use label quality and annotation to turn a vague quality claim into an observable criterion. Define a representative dataset, an expected outcome or rubric, a baseline, and the failure categories you will record; interpret aggregate scores alongside examples and affected groups.

content.task: Practice data collection and source selection within data preparation and quality: use a small synthetic input, predict the result, run the example, then change one input to test an edge case. Record the expected result and one limitation.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example uses a clearly described, non-sensitive input.
Expected behavior and at least one edge/failure case are written down.
The learner checks the result against an explicit criterion and records limitations.
hints: Begin with a tiny input whose expected behavior you can explain before running it.
Change one variable at a time and retain a fixed baseline for comparison.
When a model or external service is involved, inspect evidence and errors; do not treat the model response as a trusted instruction.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assuming fluent or plausible output is necessarily correct.
common_mistakes.fix: Use evidence, schema checks, representative test cases, and human review for consequential results.

common_mistakes.mistake: Changing several inputs or parameters at once.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep a baseline and vary one factor at a time so the effect can be interpreted.

common_mistakes.mistake: Putting secrets or private source material in prompts, logs, or a public example.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic data, server-side secret storage, data minimization, and reviewed retention rules.

summary: Data Preparation and Quality is one part of a larger generative AI application lifecycle.
